GENERAL SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. A mixture of two liquids

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cell division? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell division.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cell division.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cell division.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Cell division.

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Carbon and its Oxides? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Carbon and its Oxides.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Carbon and its Oxides.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Carbon and its Oxides.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Carbon and its Oxides.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Polymers? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Polymers.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Polymers.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Polymers.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Polymers.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters.? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..

9. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Ecosystems? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Ecosystems.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Ecosystems.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Ecosystems.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Ecosystems.

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

12. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Only carbon dioxide

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Electrostatics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Current Electricity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Motion 3.5 Electromagnetic Spectrum Page 12 of  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Mains Electricity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — 100 °C

2. C — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. A — Ice melting to water

4. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell division.

5. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Carbon and its Oxides.

7. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Polymers.

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters..

9. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

10. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Ecosystems.

11. A — Producers

12. A — Glucose and oxygen
